newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian president fights four in November poll.
newsitem.headline: Zambian president fights four in November poll.

text.p: Zambian President Frederick Chiluba will fight four challengers in November 18 elections from which he has banned his main rival, Kenneth Kaunda, officials said on Monday.

"I have received valid nomination papers from five candidates," Chief Justice Mathew Ngulube, returning officer for the presidential elections, told reporters after the deadline for applications passed.

Kaunda, who ruled Zambia for 27 years from independence from Britain until Chiluba won first free elections in 1991, is the strongest opposition candidate but was barred from standing by constitutional changes that have angered foreign aid donors.
He said last week his United National Independence Party would boycott parallel parliamentary elections in the copper-rich country, which he said were a sham.

Chiluba's rivals will be Dean Mungomba (Zambian Democratic Congress), Humphrey Mulemba (National Party), Akashambatwa Mbikusita Lewanika (Agenda for Zambia) and Chama Chakomboka (Movement for Democratic Process).
Political analysts say none of them pose a major threat to Chiluba at present, though Mbikusita Lewanika's party is only a week old and little-known.
All the challengers bar Chakomboka were former ministers in Chiluba's cabinet who resigned or were sacked.
Kaunda is banned from standing because he has already served as president more than twice and has non-Zambian parents.

The constitutional changes this year which ruled him out were widely criticised by donor nations, who had five years ago praised the advent of democracy to Zambia, as a deliberate move by Chiluba to ensure he held on to power.
Six other parties are also boycotting the poll.
